ruledBy: Astra editorial review, adopted as Al's ruling (his instruction, 2026-09-05; veto list: none)
note: KEEP and FIX (fixed wording) are kept. KILL is held as `unruled`, NOT rejected — Al ruled that explicitly, so no downstream step may treat a KILL as struck. New-lines CSV rows are kept with source astra-new. astraTime is Astra's own visual reading of the hour and does not override the photograph's rotation slot.

kept.text: Somebody's weather report just got a lot longer.
kept.fixedFrom: Somewhere a weather reporter is living their best life.

kept.text: So much for that expensive alarm clock.
Breakfast first. Checking the roof can wait.

unruled.text: Lightning over the skyline and brake lights all the way in: Joburg is up early.
unruled.reason: R1 and R5 fail: location-specific skyline and traffic inventory.

unruled.text: The slow lane, the fast lane, and the sky lane — only one is moving.
unruled.reason: R5 and R7 fail: invented sky lane captions traffic and lightning.

kept.text: Every dog in the suburb filed a report at the same instant.
The dog has told the whole street about this.
You heard it. The dog is making absolutely sure.

unruled.text: That one landed close enough to count the seconds on one hand.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: describes the pictured strike through its apparent distance.

unruled.text: The whole street went daylight for a quarter of a second.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: retells the visible flash.

kept.text: You can get up now and inspect yesterday's optimism.
Morning jobs. Start by finding the washing line.

unruled.text: Those bubble clouds are the storm's signature, written on the way out.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: explains the cloud formation poetically.

unruled.text: That is the back page of a storm, and it reads better than the front.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: literary storm caption without an ordinary consequence.

unruled.text: The windpomp has seen a thousand of these and still stopped to look.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: gives the pictured windpump an impossible reaction.

kept.text: Your dog would like breakfast delivered for once.
You slept well. The dog has a different account.

unruled.text: The storm passed an hour ago; the news has not reached under the bed yet.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: delayed-news joke still describes the hiding dog.

unruled.text: The sky has moved on. The dachshund is requesting written confirmation.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: amusing bureaucracy still captions this dachshund.

unruled.text: The dog's under the bed. Smart move, honestly.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: directly describes the dog's visible hiding place.

kept.text: You can wait. Your shopping has nowhere else to be.
kept.fixedFrom: The gap between flashes is being counted by everyone under this roof.

kept.text: You only popped out for milk and now have friends.
Shopping done. Apparently you're staying for tea.

unruled.text: The trolleys are staying exactly where the storm interrupted them.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: describes the abandoned trolleys.

unruled.text: Five strangers, one roof, one unspoken agreement: not yet.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: headcount and imagined agreement caption the sheltering group.

kept.text: Mum would like her concerns put in writing.
Plans cancelled. You seem surprisingly relieved.

unruled.text: That sky would send most people home; it is sending him in.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: narrates the surfer's pictured direction.

unruled.text: The storm is doing the wave-making and he is doing the arithmetic.
unruled.reason: R1 and R5 fail: condition opener explains the surfer's activity.

unruled.text: Big sky, bigger sea, one board: the argument for staying home lost.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: scenic inventory supplies the entire argument.

kept.text: Your cheapest umbrella has explained its price.
Walk postponed. The apology can happen by phone.

unruled.text: The umbrella is now a diagram of an umbrella.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: clever visual comparison remains an umbrella caption.

unruled.text: Leaves in the street, spokes in the air: the storm is winning on all fronts.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: inventories leaves and umbrella spokes.

unruled.text: The wind has a personal vendetta against umbrellas.
unruled.reason: R1 and R5 fail: condition opener explains the broken umbrella.

kept.text: Just one last job before home, you said.
Home soon. You have stopped putting a time on it.

unruled.text: That storm is twenty minutes out and both of them know the maths.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: narrates the loaders and invents a precise deadline.

unruled.text: The sky set the deadline; the bakkie gets loaded to it.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: describes the pictured loading race.

unruled.text: The mountains are already getting theirs; this hay has about twenty minutes.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: landscape caption invents a twenty-minute forecast.

kept.text: Sorry, what? An excellent evening not to have heard.
Supper inside. Somebody still has to clear a table.

unruled.text: The balcony beats the couch when the sky is doing this.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: merely endorses the pictured viewing position.

unruled.text: Sunset on one side, artillery on the other, and she has the balcony.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: dramatic sunset-and-lightning inventory.

unruled.text: The storm is doing the rounds of the suburbs and saving town for last.
unruled.reason: R1 and R5 fail: condition opener invents a local storm route.

kept.text: Your candles may finally justify that drawer.
Dinner for two. Torch for one.

unruled.text: Candles in the windows: the storm has already had a word with the power.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: explains the pictured window lights through an assumed outage.

unruled.text: The palms are pointing the way the storm is going, which is this way.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: describes the palm direction.

unruled.text: Lightning inside the cloud: the storm is still deciding where to put it.
unruled.reason: R1 and R5 fail: lightning description adds no human consequence.

kept.text: Nobody believed you fancied an evening walk anyway.
Going out tonight. As far as the gate, perhaps.

unruled.text: The sea is taking the strikes tonight so the land doesn't have to.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: scenery personification implies unjustified protection for land.

unruled.text: Sunset tried to happen; the storm had other bookings for that sky.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: booking metaphor remains a sky caption.

unruled.text: The waves were the show until the sky decided otherwise.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: merely swaps two visible spectacles.

kept.text: Your landlord is about to hear from you again.
Quiet evening. You should have said it softly.

unruled.text: The roof has an opinion tonight and the bucket is taking minutes.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: meeting metaphor captions the roof leak and bucket.

unruled.text: One drip, one bucket, one towel: the storm has made it indoors, barely.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: counts the pictured leak-management objects.

unruled.text: Somewhere up there the rain found a way in, and it is being managed.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: explains the leak already shown.

kept.text: The strike lasted half a second; the video will last the whole group chat.
You filmed for ten minutes. You missed it.
kept.fixedFrom: The sky does one take and expects you to be ready.

kept.text: Muting the family chat until breakfast seems fair.
Phone charged. Nobody has asked for your video yet.

unruled.text: Every South African storm gets filmed vertical, and this one earned it.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: directly captions the pictured phone recording.

kept.text: You can skip the run with a clear conscience.
kept.fixedFrom: The sky is loading something and the question is whether it lands mid-run.

kept.text: Your exercise excuse has finally arrived on time.
Shoes on. A remarkable waste of effort.

unruled.text: Warm-up done; now he is waiting on a ruling from upstairs.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: captions the runner's visible wait.

unruled.text: Hands on hips: the international sign for arguing with weather.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: explicitly explains the pictured hands-on-hips pose.

kept.text: Your first coffee deserves your undivided attention.
Up early. Not quite by choice.

unruled.text: The storm is keeping to the mountains, and the stoep is keeping the view.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: mountain-view commentary, no human consequence.

unruled.text: First coffee of the day, best show of the week, same ten minutes.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: coffee-and-view caption offers scenic appreciation.

unruled.text: The rain has been and gone; the electricity is still saying goodbye.
unruled.reason: R1 and R5 fail: weather recap replaces ordinary life.

kept.text: Perhaps start the day with a less confident plan.
Breakfast first. The rest is now negotiable.

unruled.text: That horizon is half sunset, half warning, and the bakkie knows the difference.
unruled.reason: R5 and R6 fail: horizon caption imposes sunset on dawn.

unruled.text: Dust now, mud by dark — that cloud bank is not decoration.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: describes dust and clouds, then predicts mud.

unruled.text: The mealies have been waiting for that cloud longer than anyone in the bakkie.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: romanticises the pictured crop and vehicle.

kept.text: The eighteenth can wait; the sky is playing through.
Your scorecard can stop getting worse now.
kept.fixedFrom: That is the course's way of saying the round is over.

kept.text: Finally, a respectable excuse for your scorecard.
Clubs packed. Your pride gets to come home intact.

unruled.text: Two club selections left: the clubhouse or the car.
unruled.reason: R7 fails: club double meaning carries the whole joke.

kept.text: Kickoff is under review by the only official that outranks the referee.
Your team has found someone else to blame for once.
Match delayed. Everyone is suddenly a forecaster.

unruled.text: The floodlights are on; the sky brought its own anyway.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: describes floodlights and lightning.

unruled.text: The pitch is ready, the lines are marked, and the weather has the whistle.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: pitch inventory delays a familiar personification.

kept.text: Best greet the neighbour before asking for things back.
Chores postponed. Several new ones are on the way.

unruled.text: The storm rearranged the stoep furniture and did not ask anybody first.
unruled.reason: R1 and R5 fail: condition opener describes toppled furniture.

unruled.text: The chairs are down, the branches are down, and the sky is not done.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: inventories the visible damage.

unruled.text: Every loose object in the garden has chosen violence.
unruled.reason: R5 and R7 fail: borrowed internet phrasing captions scattered objects.

kept.text: You can explain your plans to someone who listens.
Jobs listed. Best put a pencil next to them.

unruled.text: He has seen fifty of these arrive, and he still comes out to watch.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: invents a spectator's history instead of addressing the reader.

unruled.text: Dust first, rain second: the order of business is written on the horizon.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: literal weather sequence in business language.

unruled.text: The drought and the storm are about to have a word, and he wants to hear it.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: landscape drama narrates the spectator's supposed interest.

kept.text: Even the hadedas are quiet.
Could we discuss the plan with fewer outdoor bits?
Everyone inside. The argument fits in here too.

unruled.text: The street cleared out early; only the hadeda is finishing its rounds.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: narrates the empty street and pictured bird.

unruled.text: The sky is stacking up over the dorp and even the palm has gone still.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: cloud-and-palm description depends on the scene.

kept.text: Your weekend now includes everybody else's branches.
kept.fixedFrom: The storm made one pass and left the street a week of gardening.

kept.text: Your quiet evening now includes a call to the roofer.
Home early. You may wish you hadn't been.

unruled.text: Branches down, lights on, storm gone: the after-party is all admin.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: damage inventory buries the useful aftermath.

unruled.text: The sunset is back like nothing happened; the trees know otherwise.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: personified sunset and trees remain a landscape caption.

kept.text: Your video won't settle the argument about the size.
kept.fixedFrom: That strike will look half this size on the phone, and he knows it.

kept.text: Your family has already seen three videos like yours.
Phone away. You can watch the next one yourself.

unruled.text: Two strikes in one frame: the sky is doing his content for him.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: describes the photographed strikes and recording.

unruled.text: Rain on the railing, lightning on the horizon, phone doing its best.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: inventory of railing, lightning and phone.

kept.text: Thirst has been replaced as the bedtime excuse.
Bedtime again. Nobody seems to have heard you.

unruled.text: First storm he has stayed up for, and the sky is making it count.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: invents the pictured child's first-storm history.

unruled.text: Thunder is scary from bed and magnificent from a window; he moved.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: narrates the child's pictured move to the window.

unruled.text: The best television in the house is currently the weather.
unruled.reason: R2 and R5 fail: familiar spectacle-as-television stock caption.

kept.text: Your home repair list has requested an urgent update.
Romance later. First find something absorbent.

unruled.text: The storm found the ceiling's weak spot; the bucket arrived three drops later.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: gives timing to the pictured leak response.

unruled.text: The rain is now technically a house guest, and it chose the main bedroom.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: house-guest joke still describes the bedroom leak.

unruled.text: Leak over the bed, laughter over the leak: married storm protocol.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: inventories leak and laughter, then labels the marriage.

kept.text: Your favourite parking spot has lost its appeal.
Car covered. You could do with the same treatment.

unruled.text: Hail on the way down and a tarp halfway on: this one is going to be close.
unruled.reason: R1 and R5 fail: condition opener narrates the tarp race.

unruled.text: The sky is throwing ice and he is answering with a tarp.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: describes the man covering his load.

unruled.text: Hail gives you about ninety seconds of warning, and he is using all of them.
unruled.reason: R1 and R5 fail: unsupported warning time captions the worker.

kept.text: Your lap is now reserved for the entire dog.
kept.fixedFrom: One flash outside and the seating plan changed itself.

kept.text: You can be brave once the dog believes you.
Lap available. Terms now set by the dog.

unruled.text: The spot under the table was chosen scientifically: furthest from the sky.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: invented scientific rationale captions the dog's hiding place.

unruled.text: Thunder counts double when you have ears like that.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: directly points at the pictured dog's ears.

kept.text: Your batting average survives another day.
kept.fixedFrom: Bad light stopped play, then the light got a lot worse.

kept.text: Try the coach now; your excuse has improved.
Practice cancelled. Try looking less pleased.

unruled.text: The covers made it on; the kit did not make it off.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: describes the visible pitch covers and abandoned kit.

unruled.text: A sky that colour clears a cricket field faster than any umpire.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: explains the empty cricket field.

kept.text: Your plastic chairs may visit before you do.
Visitors postponed. The furniture may still go.

unruled.text: The first casualty is a plastic chair, and the storm is not even here yet.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: narrates the pictured fallen chair.

unruled.text: That rain on the horizon is about ten minutes from this puddle.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: scene description invents a precise arrival time.

unruled.text: The wind came through first and signed its work with one white chair.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: signature metaphor describes the fallen white chair.

kept.text: Your evening braai has acquired an indoor committee.
Guests at six. Best revise what you promised them.

unruled.text: The umbrella is coming down in the storm's final two minutes of notice.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: narrates the umbrella action and invents its deadline.

unruled.text: Half the sky is still summer; the other half is why he is hurrying.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: sky commentary explains the pictured man's hurry.

unruled.text: Leaves already sideways: the storm sent its calling card ahead.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: describes the blowing leaves.

kept.text: At last, a break from being asked to stop the car.
Keys ready. No particular hurry to use them.

unruled.text: The car is the best hide this country makes for lightning season.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: car-watching caption makes an unnecessary blanket safety claim.

unruled.text: Rain on the glass, bolt in the frame, and not one drop on the photographer.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: inventories rain, lightning and photographer.

unruled.text: Front-row seats, full cover, wipers off: storm-watching done properly.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: describes and endorses the pictured viewing arrangement.

kept.text: Your dog has cancelled sleeping in its own bed.
Goodnight, then. Apparently that was optimistic.

unruled.text: The rain is coming through the streetlight at forty-five degrees, which means wind joined in.
unruled.reason: R1 and R5 fail: condition opener explains the rain's visible angle.

unruled.text: Lightning behind the cloud: the storm is working with the lights off.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: describes hidden lightning through a work metaphor.

unruled.text: That old tree has stood through a hundred of these and is counting this one too.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: scenic tree biography, no human consequence.

kept.text: Your roof repair savings have been noticed.
Sleep first. Tomorrow has acquired a few expenses.

unruled.text: The gutter gave up on the downpipe and started its own waterfall.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: waterfall personification explains the overflowing gutter.

unruled.text: Purple sky, purple petals: the storm colour-matched the driveway tonight.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: describes the pictured colour palette.

unruled.text: The overflow says the roof got a month of rain in one evening.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: runoff caption invents a month's rainfall comparison.

kept.text: Nobody's leaving; find the good biscuits.
Bedtime soon. The house has some final remarks.

unruled.text: The roof has no gutter on that side and tonight it is a waterfall.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: literal roof-runoff description.

unruled.text: Rain coming off the roof in one solid sheet: the stoep has a curtain tonight.
unruled.reason: R1 and R5 fail: condition opener leads to a visual simile.

unruled.text: Everything past the gate is weather; everything inside it is fine.
unruled.reason: R2 and R5 fail: cosy stock-photo reassurance, no earned turn.

kept.text: Your neighbours now know what your pyjamas look like.
Everyone awake. Nobody admits they got a fright.

unruled.text: The whole sky went mauve for a second and the street pretended not to notice.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: colour commentary personifies the pictured street.

unruled.text: One streetlight versus the entire electrical budget of that cloud.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: electrical-budget metaphor describes lights in the image.

unruled.text: That flash reached town before its thunder; the gap is closing though.
unruled.reason: R5 fails: lightning timing explanation offers no ordinary-life joke.
